sources.title: Richard S. Sutton and Andrew G. Barto, Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction, 2nd ed.
sources.locator: §5.5, printed pp. 128–132 (Stanford PDF pp. 140–145): behavior/target distinction, action coverage, trajectory ratios (5.3), ordinary estimates (5.4), weighted estimates (5.5), finite-sample bias and the loop variance calculation in Example 5.5.

contents.name: Behavior and target policies, action coverage, and the product trajectory ratio, §5.5
contents.reason: The book supplies the discrete stationary-policy convention and action-ratio motivation. The local definition distinguishes full finite-horizon trajectory absolute continuity from the sufficient pointwise action-overlap condition.

contents.name: Ordinary trajectory importance sampling and weighted importance sampling, equations (5.3)–(5.5)
contents.reason: The procedures and zero-denominator convention are used as context; the finite-horizon measure-theoretic ratio and unbiasedness proof are local.

contents.name: The weighted one-sample estimate and ordinary-versus-weighted finite-sample behavior, §5.5
contents.reason: The example recomputes a finite-horizon sample bias and a separate clipping bias exactly; no general finite-sample unbiasedness claim is imported.

contents.name: Ordinary importance sampling loop example and expected-square calculation, Example 5.5
contents.reason: The source motivates multiplicative variance growth. The authored example uses a different fixed finite horizon and computes its exact finite variance locally.

contents.name: Ordinary estimator expectation under target coverage, §5.5
contents.reason: The source states the discrete change-of-policy identity; the local theorem proves both full-trajectory and prefix identities under the exact finite-horizon hypotheses.

recovery_attempts.outcome: The complete 352-page Stanford-hosted book PDF opened successfully; §5.5 and Example 5.5 were inspected at the stated printed and PDF locators.

sources.title: Nan Jiang and Lihong Li, Doubly Robust Off-policy Value Evaluation for Reinforcement Learning, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 48
sources.locator: Complete 10-page ICML 2016 paper; §§3.2.1–3.3 and 4.1–4.2, printed/PDF pp. 2–4: finite-horizon return, trajectory and step-wise IS, WIS, contextual-bandit DR, sequential recursion (10), and Theorem 1.

contents.name: Finite-horizon trajectory setup, target value, Bellman value model, and IS estimators, §3.2 and equations (1)–(7)
contents.reason: The paper supplies finite-horizon estimator conventions. The local statement separates its exact ratio assumptions from its self-normalized estimator.

contents.name: Sequential doubly robust recursion and target-policy value-model convention, §4.1 equation (10)
contents.reason: The local algorithm gives the equivalent finite-horizon residual sum with an explicit terminal value and sample-fixed nuisance inputs.

contents.name: Theorem 1 unbiasedness statement and its finite-horizon conditions, §4.2
contents.reason: The proceedings text states unbiasedness but does not supply the complete two-branch proof; the local theorem proves the exact correct-ratio and correct-model branches independently.

contents.name: Weighted importance sampling is described as biased and consistent, §3.2.2
contents.reason: Only finite-sample bias is used; no asymptotic consistency claim is made.

recovery_attempts.outcome: The complete 10-page PMLR PDF opened successfully; §§3.2–4.2 and the paper's conclusion were inspected. The paper notes a deferred Appendix A proof but the fetched proceedings text contains no complete proof of the unbiasedness assertion.

sources.title: Sergey Levine, Aviral Kumar, George Tucker, and Justin Fu, Offline Reinforcement Learning: Tutorial, Review, and Perspectives on Open Problems
sources.locator: Complete 43-page 2020 review; §2.4 (distribution shift), §3.1 and equations (5)–(6) (OPE and doubly robust estimation), §3.5, §§4.3–4.4 (policy constraints and uncertainty), and §5.1 (model exploitation).

contents.name: Offline distribution shift and missing data coverage, §2.4
contents.reason: The review motivates the information limitation; the exact two-MDP indistinguishability proof is new and complete.

contents.name: Trajectory IS, self-normalized WIS, per-decision IS, and DR, §3.1
contents.reason: This source is a tutorial overview; all estimator identities used as theorem claims are proved locally.

contents.name: The DR alternative between correct behavior propensities and a correct model, §3.1
contents.reason: The review supports the intended two-branch scope but is not treated as proof of the finite-horizon identity.

contents.name: Policy constraints, uncertainty estimates, and model exploitation, §§4.3–4.4 and 5.1
contents.reason: The remark preserves the source's caution that these are mitigation strategies, not a generic offline-RL safety or performance guarantee.

recovery_attempts.outcome: The complete arXiv PDF was located from the arXiv record; the full-text review HTML and the design-designated sections were inspected.
